# Four consolidation strands — student workbook
Use fictional data and supplied offline files. Show prediction, attempt, tests, explanation and a changed retry. Most teaching is a sample/repair sequence; teacher chooses depth to fit eight lessons. These tasks sample Year12 Units3–4 and revisit earlier foundations; they are not every syllabus point.

## A. Python, structures, algorithms and objects
A1: Repair aliased grid creation; implement row_totals for a rectangular list of lists of non-negative integer counts. Contract: [] -> []; [[],[]] -> [0,0]; reject ragged grids, negatives, floats and bools. Test no mutation. Explain nested traversal and linear growth in cell count. Revisit values/loops/functions when these are the cause.
A2: Implement binary search returning any matching index, or -1. Sorted comparable input is a precondition; do not claim sortedness validation/sorting itself is O(log n). Trace found and missing targets; test empty, first,last and duplicates. Compare one unsorted search with many searches on sorted maintained data. Implement stable insertion sort on a shallow copy; trace [5,2,4,2], explain best/worst comparisons and contrast bubble/selection without claiming all versions share stability or early exit.
A3: Implement Session(capacity), remaining, reserve and location; subclass OnlineSession overrides location, use one loop to invoke both. Reject bad capacity and reservation beyond full. Explain inheritance, polymorphism, method responsibility and the limits of underscore attributes. Class validation is not cross-process concurrency or DB enforcement. Add a test then diagnose a deliberately faulty boundary `<0` instead of `<=0`.

## B. Relational design, SQL and evidence
Fresh five-table equipment seed: Category,Resource,Member,Loan,Inspection. Draw crow's-foot PK/FK relationships, optional loan ReturnDate, and zero/many loans/inspections per resource. LoanID identifies repeated loan events; a resource/person pair alone does not uniquely identify repeated lending. Normalise a flat sheet using LoanID->ResourceID,MemberID,dates; ResourceID->Label,CategoryID; CategoryID->Name; MemberID->Name. Explain transitive dependencies; with single-column LoanID there is no partial-key dependency of that key.
B1: Report ALL resources with total and active loans. Active means an actual Loan row with NULL ReturnDate. Predict R04 before SQL. Explain why COUNT(CASE...THEN LoanID END) avoids counting an outer placeholder; a CASE that returns1 for NULL date alone does not.
B2: Four-table active-loan label: Member.Name concatenated ' / ' Resource.Label, category name, sorted member/resource. Explain filtering and join grain. Joining inspections to loans can multiply rows; plan aggregation per entity before joining separate one-to-many sets.
B3: Demonstrate invalid Passed2, orphan Loan and rollback on an in-memory copy. Check protected data and PK/FK/domain rules. Positive values and date text do not ensure chronology or one active loan per resource. Propose a concurrency test/implementation rule rather than claiming constraints solve it. Explain DB-API versus ODBC and saved restore/reopen evidence.

## C. Networks and protocols
C1: Allocate conventional IPv4 subnets from192.168.40.0/24 for60,28,12hosts, largest first. Include prefix,network,hostrange,broadcast,gateway,capacity; avoid overlap. Explain IPv6 has no broadcast and that ordinary IPv6 LAN planning isn't this IPv4 usable-host subtraction exercise.
C2: For client192.168.40.10/26 to remote documentation address203.0.113.20, trace DNS lookup, TCP establishment and TLS/application traffic as a simplified example. Explain first-hop gateway/frame vs routed IP addressing, layer roles and address changes at hops/NAT where relevant. UDP lacks TCP's built-in reliability; an application such as QUIC can add reliability. A port alone is not protocol/security evidence.
C3: Hostname resolution fails but a separately verified connection to the intended IP/service succeeds. State DNS hypothesis, alternative, precise next check and observation needed. Do not treat ping failure as definitive service failure. Draw a course-convention network diagram with guest/staff separation, router/firewall role, switch and server; segmentation needs a policy at the actual boundary. No real school configuration/scanning.

## D. Security, cryptography and responsibility
D1: Fictional future app permits browser-supplied role='Registrar'. Identify CIA/AAA mechanism, trustworthy evidence, preventive/detective/recovery controls and legitimate/prohibited acceptance tests. Red proposes paper failure; blue proposes control/detection; record authorised scope/stop condition. Distinguish labels/IPs from identity.
D2: Explain certificate trust/server private proof, authenticated ephemeral agreement and symmetric authenticated records for simplified TLS1.3. Distinguish hash/signature/encryption. VPN tunnel and at-rest protection have different boundaries; endpoint/permission weaknesses remain.
D3: For an explicitly assumed private APP entity, map collection notice, overseas disclosure, stale data, protected retention and verified access to APP5/8/10/11/12. Explain prompt assessment and missing eligibility facts;30days isn't a blanket notification delay. WA public-sector counterfactual needs separate framework/date: July2026 substantive privacy provisions; January2027 state breach notification commencement. Evaluate mining bias, pseudonymisation, source ownership/acknowledgement and suitable release permission. No real personal data or regulator notices.
